enzyme_name: unknown (no characterised linatine synthase)
organism_context: Linum usitatissimum (flaxseed) is the source of linatine, a gamma-glutamyl-1-amino-D-proline vitamin B6 antagonist
rationale: No enzyme has been assigned to this condensation; KEGG itself annotates R02895 as 'unclear reaction / incomplete reaction' (no water or cofactor balance), and literature searches return no linatine biosynthetic enzyme.
direction_note: The reaction as encoded is not a real elementary step (D-proline + Gln -> linatine with only protons released), so neither direction call rests on enzymology; the disagreement is an artefact of an incomplete KEGG stub.

enzyme_name: sphingolipid C4-hydroxylase/Delta4-desaturase (DES2/DEGS2); paralogue DES1/DEGS1 is desaturase-only
organism_context: Mouse/human; DES2 is the intestine- and kidney-enriched paralogue, DES1 is ubiquitous. The Drosophila ancestor (degenerative spermatocyte-1, des-1) is desaturase-only.
rationale: Mouse DES2/DEGS2 is a single polypeptide with two genuine catalytic outputs on the same sphinganine substrate - C-4 hydroxylation to phytosphingosine and Delta4 desaturation to sphingosine (Omae et al.); the paralogue DES1 performs only the desaturation, so the bifunctional assignment holds for DES2 and the reaction can also be run by a monofunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Both activities are O2/cytochrome-b5-coupled oxidations that are effectively irreversible in the desaturation direction, supporting the LLM '>' call; ModelSEED's '<' comes from treating the oxidant as a free FAD/FADH2 couple, which is not the physiological electron acceptor.

enzyme_name: 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase (3-MST)
organism_context: Human/mammalian MPST and bacterial SseA; the protein has two tandem rhodanese-homology domains but only the C-terminal one carries the catalytic cysteine
rationale: 3-MST runs a single ping-pong sulfurtransfer chemistry via an enzyme-cysteine persulfide; the various reported outputs (thiosulfate with sulfite, H2S/persulfides with thioredoxin or other thiophilic acceptors) are the same catalytic activity with different sulfur acceptors, and the N-terminal rhodanese domain is non-catalytic.
direction_note: The physiological flux is mercaptopyruvate + sulfite -> pyruvate + thiosulfate (the LLM's '>'), and it is pulled irreversibly by the loss of the thioester-like sulfur and by rapid downstream consumption of pyruvate; ModelSEED's '<' would require thiosulfate to re-sulfurate pyruvate, which 3-MST does not do.

enzyme_name: Renilla luciferin (coelenterazine) sulfotransferase / luciferin sulfokinase
organism_context: Anthozoan sea pansies Renilla reniformis and R. muelleri; multiple cytosolic sulfotransferase isoforms, recombinantly expressed in E. coli
rationale: The cloned R. muelleri enzymes are ordinary single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferases with one PAPS-dependent sulfuryl-transfer activity; no second catalytic function has been reported.
direction_note: This is the clearest direction case in the chunk: the enzyme's physiological job is the REVERSE of the written sulfation - it uses PAP to desulfate stored luciferyl sulfate and release free coelenterazine for the luciferase flash, so ModelSEED's '<' matches the in vivo role even though the generic sulfotransferase convention (and the LLM) favours '>'.

enzyme_name: short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (2-methylbutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase, SBCAD)
organism_context: Human mitochondrial matrix; homotetrameric FAD flavoprotein of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family, isoleucine catabolism
rationale: ACADSB encodes a single-activity FAD-dependent alpha,beta-dehydrogenase; its deficiency (2-methylbutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency / 2-methylbutyrylglycinuria) is a clean single-enzyme defect with no second catalytic activity reported.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases are committed to the oxidative direction because electrons leave via ETF -> ETF-QO -> ubiquinone rather than to a free FADH2 pool; ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of balancing the half-reaction on free FAD/FADH2, and no enzyme reduces tiglyl-CoA back to 2-methylbutyryl-CoA in this pathway.

enzyme_name: pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase (P5CR), acting on 3-hydroxy-L-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate
organism_context: Ubiquitous; KEGG assigns R03291 to KO K00286 (pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase, EC 1.5.1.2). The oxidative counterpart in hydroxyproline catabolism is a different protein (PRODH2/HYPDH, FAD-linked).
rationale: The NAD(H)-linked half of EC 1.5.1.2 is pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase, a single-activity NAD(P)H oxidoreductase; the genuine catabolic hydroxyproline dehydrogenase is the separate FAD enzyme PRODH2, so the pyridine-nucleotide form of this reaction belongs to the reductase.
direction_note: This is a real enzymology split: P5CR runs reductively (3-hydroxy-P5C + NADH -> hydroxyproline), which matches ModelSEED's '<', while the oxidative direction the LLM picked is carried in vivo by FAD-dependent PRODH2/HYPDH, not by any NAD-linked enzyme.

enzyme_name: pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase (P5CR), NADPH form, acting on 3-hydroxy-L-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate
organism_context: Ubiquitous; the NADPH-preferring isoforms of P5CR cover the EC 1.5.1.2 NADP variant of the same chemistry
rationale: Same single-activity NAD(P)H-dependent reductase as rxn02356, differing only in pyridine nucleotide preference; no second catalytic activity is fused to P5CR in any lineage I could find.
direction_note: As for rxn02356, P5CR physiologically reduces 3-hydroxy-P5C to trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline (ModelSEED's '<'); the oxidative '>' direction is the job of the FAD/quinone-linked hydroxyproline dehydrogenase, a different protein.

enzyme_name: hydroxyproline dehydrogenase (HYPDH / proline dehydrogenase 2; bacterial LhpD)
organism_context: Human/mouse mitochondrial PRODH2 and bacterial LhpD; KEGG maps R03295 to K11394, EC 1.5.5.3 (quinone acceptor)
rationale: PRODH2 was shown to be a dedicated FAD-dependent hydroxyproline dehydrogenase (not a proline dehydrogenase), carrying one catalytic activity on a single flavoprotein chain; unlike the fused bacterial PutA it has no attached P5C-dehydrogenase domain.
direction_note: The flavin/quinone-linked enzyme runs only oxidatively (hydroxyproline -> 3-hydroxy-P5C) in collagen/hydroxyproline catabolism, so the LLM's '>' is right for this FAD variant even though the sibling NAD(P) reactions (rxn02356/02358) genuinely run the other way.

enzyme_name: none - non-enzymatic hydration/ring opening of prostacyclin
organism_context: Mammalian vasculature; PGI2 is chemically unstable at physiological pH with a half-life of minutes
rationale: KEGG annotates R03521 explicitly as 'non-enzymatic' and 'multi-step'; the enol-ether of PGI2 hydrolyses spontaneously to 6-keto-PGF1alpha, so there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: The spontaneous hydrolysis runs only toward 6-keto-PGF1alpha (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require dehydrating the open-chain ketone back into the strained bicyclic enol ether, which does not happen, so this is a straightforward ModelSEED direction error.

enzyme_name: haloalkane dehalogenase (alkylhalidase)
organism_context: Bacterial: Xanthobacter autotrophicus DhlA, Rhodococcus DhaA, Sphingobium LinB, plus rhizobial homologues; KEGG assigns R03523 to EC 3.8.1.5 rather than ModelSEED's 3.8.1.1
rationale: Haloalkane dehalogenases are single-domain alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold enzymes with one Asp-His-Asp/Glu catalytic machinery performing SN2 displacement plus hydrolysis of the covalent alkyl-enzyme; broad halide/substrate promiscuity is one active site, not a second activity.
direction_note: Hydrolytic C-halogen cleavage is essentially irreversible (halide release plus hydration of the resulting carbinol to formaldehyde), so the LLM's '>' is correct; ModelSEED's '<' would mean synthesising a C-Br bond from free bromide, which no hydrolase does.

enzyme_name: nitrilase (alpha-aminopropiononitrile aminohydrolase)
organism_context: Bacterial, fungal and plant nitrilases (KEGG KO K01501); helical homo-oligomers assembled from dimers
rationale: Nitrilases use a single Glu-Lys-Cys catalytic triad and one thioimidate intermediate to take the nitrile all the way to acid + ammonia; the minor amide released by some nitrilases is an intermediate partition product of that same site, not a second catalytic activity (and the nitrile hydratase + amidase route is two separate proteins).
direction_note: Nitrile hydrolysis to a carboxylate plus ammonia is thermodynamically one-way, so '>' (the LLM call) is right; ModelSEED's '<' would require dehydrating alanine into a nitrile, which is not biochemistry this enzyme performs.

enzyme_name: UDP-glucose:vitexin 2''-O-beta-D-glucosyltransferase (vitexin beta-glucosyltransferase)
organism_context: Plant (flavone C-glycoside-accumulating species such as Avena and Silene); EC 2.4.1.105 is known only as a partially purified activity - no gene has been cloned, and KEGG assigns no KO
rationale: The activity is a plant family-1 UGT-type single-domain GT-B glycosyltransferase with one sugar-transfer activity; the classification is inferred from the enzyme class rather than from a characterised protein, since the gene has never been identified.
direction_note: Glycosyl transfer from the activated donor UDP-glucose is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way in biosynthesis, favouring the LLM's '>'; ModelSEED's '<' would make the enzyme a UDP-dependent deglucosylase, which family-1 UGTs are not.

enzyme_name: unknown (no single enzyme converts free ferulate to scopoletin)
organism_context: Plant phenylpropanoid/coumarin branch (Arabidopsis, Ipomoea, Morinda)
rationale: Scopoletin is made from feruloyl-CoA by the 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase F6'H1 followed by spontaneous trans/cis isomerisation and lactonisation (with CoA release), i.e. at least a CoA-ligase plus a dioxygenase plus non-enzymatic steps; the ModelSEED/KEGG stub R03580 lumps all of this into one unbalanced ferulate -> scopoletin step with no enzyme assignment.
direction_note: Because the entry is a lumped multi-step pathway and not a catalysed elementary reaction, neither direction call reflects enzymology; the real route (ferulate -> feruloyl-CoA -> scopoletin) is biosynthetically one-way, which is at least consistent with the LLM's '>'.

enzyme_name: selenophosphate synthetase (selenide, water dikinase)
organism_context: E. coli SelD and the mammalian selenoprotein SEPHS2; the paralogue SEPHS1/SPS1 has lost selenophosphate-synthesising activity and acts in a different (non-SelD) role
rationale: SelD/SEPHS2 performs one AIR-synthetase-fold phosphoryl-transfer chemistry, delivering the gamma-phosphate of ATP to selenide while hydrolysing the beta-phosphate; the duplication/subfunctionalisation history of the family produced separate proteins, not a fused bifunctional chain.
direction_note: The reaction is driven irreversibly by cleaving ATP to AMP + Pi (two phosphoanhydride bonds spent), so the LLM's '>' is clearly right; ModelSEED's '<' would have selenophosphate plus AMP plus Pi resynthesising ATP, which is thermodynamically impossible.

enzyme_name: coniferin/syringin beta-D-glucosidase (monolignol glucoside beta-glucosidase)
organism_context: Plants; Arabidopsis BGLU45/BGLU46 cluster with Pinus contorta coniferin beta-glucosidase and hydrolyse monolignol glucosides including syringin (KEGG KO K28924, EC 3.2.1.126)
rationale: These are glycoside hydrolase family 1 (clan GH-A) enzymes with a single (beta/alpha)8 barrel and one Glu/Glu acid-base + nucleophile pair; broad monolignol-glucoside specificity is one active site, not two activities.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is effectively irreversible at cellular water activity, so '>' (the LLM call) is right; the reverse glucosylation in planta is performed by a separate UDP-glucose-dependent UGT, not by running this hydrolase backwards.

enzyme_name: galactosylceramide (cerebroside) 3'-sulfotransferase, acting on galactosylsphingosine/psychosine
organism_context: Mammalian Golgi type-II membrane protein; the same enzyme sulfates GalCer, galactosylsphingosine (psychosine) and galactosylglycerolipid
rationale: The purified and later cloned PAPS:GalCer sulfotransferase carries one PAPS-binding sulfuryl-transfer site; its several lipid acceptors are substrate breadth at a single catalytic centre, not distinct activities.
direction_note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and Golgi sulfotransferases run only in the sulfating direction (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would imply PAP-dependent desulfation, which in vivo is done instead by the lysosomal hydrolase arylsulfatase A.

enzyme_name: unknown (lumped multi-enzyme sterol alkylation; sterol 24-C-methyltransferases SMT1/SMT2 plus a C-22 desaturase)
organism_context: Plants, algae and fungi; SMT1 (C-24 methylation) and SMT2 (C-24(1) methylation to the 24-ethyl series) are separate gene products, and the Delta22 bond of stigmasterol is installed by CYP710A
rationale: Converting desmosterol to stigmasterol requires two successive SAM-dependent C-alkylations on two different SMT proteins plus sterol reductase and C-22 desaturase steps, so this entry is a lumped pathway with no single catalysing enzyme; it also has no EC number or database cross-reference in the input.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible, so the biosynthetic sense is '>' , but because the entry collapses several enzymes into one step the direction conflict here is a pathway-lumping artefact rather than an enzymology question.

enzyme_name: medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD); peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1) for the EC 1.3.3.6 variant
organism_context: Human mitochondrial MCAD is a homotetrameric FAD flavoprotein; the peroxisomal alternative ACOX1 is likewise single-activity (the peroxisomal 'multifunctional enzyme' MFE-1/MFE-2 acts on the NEXT two steps, not this one)
rationale: MCAD carries one alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity per subunit and its deficiency is a clean single-enzyme inborn error; the frequently cited peroxisomal trifunctional protein is a different enzyme (hydratase/dehydrogenase/epimerase) downstream of this step.
direction_note: The dehydrogenation is pulled forward by ETF/ETF-QO handing electrons to ubiquinone, so '>' (the LLM call) is physiologically correct; ModelSEED's '<' follows from scoring the reaction against free FAD/FADH2, and reduction of (2E)-octenoyl-CoA in vivo is carried out by a separate NADPH-dependent trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase.

enzyme_name: long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD/ACADL) and very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD/ACADVL)
organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria; LCAD is a soluble homotetramer, VLCAD a membrane-associated homodimer - both single-activity flavoproteins
rationale: Recombinant human LCAD has one characterised catalytic activity (alpha,beta-dehydrogenation of long-chain acyl-CoAs, with H2O2 leakage as an uncoupling side effect rather than a second activity), and the same holds for VLCAD.
direction_note: Same as rxn02679: the ACAD step is committed forward by electron flow through ETF to the quinone pool, so the LLM's '>' matches physiology while ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of using the free FAD/FADH2 couple.

enzyme_name: N-methyltyramine N-methyltransferase (the second, distinct SAM-dependent NMT of hordenine biosynthesis)
organism_context: Hordeum vulgare (barley) seedlings; the gene has not been cloned, but the activity was chromatographically separated from the tyramine N-methyltransferase that performs the preceding step
rationale: Meyer showed that hordenine biosynthesis in barley uses TWO distinct separable SAM-dependent N-methyltransferases rather than one enzyme doing both methylations, so the protein running this step carries a single methyl-transfer activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is essentially irreversible (SAH is a poor methyl donor), so the LLM's '>' is right; ModelSEED's '<' would require SAH-dependent demethylation of hordenine, which is not a reaction this enzyme class performs.

enzyme_name: siroheme synthase CysG (precorrin-2 dehydrogenase activity); Met8p in yeast, SirC in Bacillus
organism_context: Salmonella/E. coli CysG is a trifunctional single polypeptide; Saccharomyces Met8p is bifunctional (dehydrogenase + ferrochelatase only); Bacillus megaterium SirC is a standalone monofunctional precorrin-2 dehydrogenase
rationale: In enterobacteria this NAD+-dependent precorrin-2 oxidation is one of three catalytic activities fused into the single CysG chain, with the dehydrogenase and chelatase sharing one active site distinct from the N-terminal methyltransferase site; the same step is carried by a bifunctional (Met8p) or monofunctional (SirC) protein in other lineages.
direction_note: Within CysG the sirohydrochlorin product is handed straight to the chelatase half of the same active site, so metal insertion pulls this thermodynamically marginal NAD+ oxidation forward - a concrete reason to prefer the LLM's '>' over ModelSEED's '<' here, and a textbook case of fused bifunctionality dictating direction.

enzyme_name: unknown (lumped coenzyme F430 biosynthesis: CfbA/CfbB/CfbC/CfbD/CfbE)
organism_context: Methanogenic and ANME archaea (Methanosarcina, Methanothermobacter)
rationale: Moore et al. showed F430 is built from sirohydrochlorin by five separate enzymes - CfbA (nickelochelatase), CfbB (amidase), CfbC/CfbD (reductive cyclase) and CfbE (lactamase) - so this one-step 'Ni2+ + precorrin-2 -> F430' entry has no single catalysing enzyme; it also skips the precorrin-2 -> sirohydrochlorin oxidation entirely.
direction_note: As a lumped biosynthetic pathway with ATP-dependent reductive steps it is one-way toward F430, consistent with the LLM's '>', but the direction conflict here is a pathway-lumping artefact rather than a statement about any enzyme.

enzyme_name: unknown (no enzyme reduces the nitrile of L-3-cyanoalanine to an amine)
organism_context: L-3-cyanoalanine is a plant/bacterial cyanide-detoxification product; L-2,4-diaminobutyrate is normally made from L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde by DABA aminotransferase (EctB/DabA), not from cyanoalanine
rationale: Four-electron reduction of a nitrile to a primary amine has no characterised biological catalyst, and the written equation supplies only protons with no reductant, so it is a mass-balance artefact rather than a catalysed reaction; the known fates of 3-cyanoalanine are hydration/hydrolysis to asparagine or aspartate (nitrilase/nitrile hydratase), not reduction.
direction_note: No enzyme means no enzymological basis for either call; the entry is redox-unbalanced, which is also why the thermodynamic sources agree on '<' while the LLM reads it as a biosynthetic '>'.

enzyme_name: bile salt (bile acid) sulfotransferase / hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase
organism_context: Human and rodent liver cytosol; rat BAST I and human SULT2A1 sulfate both bile acids and 3-hydroxysteroids with the same active site
rationale: Purified bile salt sulfotransferase is a single-domain cytosolic SULT with one PAPS-dependent sulfuryl-transfer activity and an ordered bi-bi mechanism; its dual bile-acid/3-hydroxysteroid acceptor range is substrate breadth, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: Sulfation from PAPS is strongly exergonic and is the detoxification/excretion direction in hepatocytes (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would amount to PAP-driven desulfation, which in vivo is instead a gut-bacterial sulfatase reaction on a different enzyme.

enzyme_name: very-long-chain / long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD, LCAD) acting on myristoyl-CoA
organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria; VLCAD is an inner-membrane-associated homodimeric FAD flavoprotein, LCAD a matrix homotetramer
rationale: Both acyl-CoA dehydrogenases that cover C14 substrates carry one catalytic activity per subunit; the multifunctional protein of long-chain beta-oxidation (mitochondrial trifunctional protein, HADHA/HADHB) acts on the three steps AFTER this dehydrogenation, not on it.
direction_note: Same mechanism as rxn02679/rxn02720: ETF-coupled electron removal commits the enzyme to the dehydrogenation direction (the LLM's '>'), while ModelSEED's '<' reflects scoring against a free FAD/FADH2 couple that the enzyme never uses.
